dateCaveat: The Hijri calendar is lunar, and an early Hijri date cannot be converted to a Gregorian one as though it had been calculated precisely from a fixed calendar; modern sources differ in how they align the two. The Gregorian dates given here are approximate.

sources.label: PBS — Muhammad: Legacy of a Prophet

eras.title: I. Before the Prophet's birth, his birth and childhood
II. The beginning of prophethood and the Meccan mission
III. The Hijrah and the founding of the community of Medina
IV. Al-Hudaybiyah, Khaybar and the international phase
V. The conquest of Mecca and its aftermath
VI. Tabuk, the Year of Delegations and the completion of the state

events.title: The standing of Quraysh and Mecca
events.summary: Mecca was an important religious and commercial centre because of the Ka'bah and its position on the trade routes. Quraysh held considerable influence over the administration of the pilgrimage and the service of the sanctuary.

events.title: The Year of the Elephant
events.summary: Abrahah, the ruler of Yemen under the Kingdom of Aksum, sent an army towards Mecca to demolish the Ka'bah. The Qur'an relates the account of the Companions of the Elephant; the army was destroyed and never reached the House.

events.title: The death of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib
events.summary: The Prophet's father died before his birth according to the best-known view. He had set out on a trading journey and fell ill in Yathrib. The Prophet was thus born fatherless.

events.title: The birth of the Prophet ﷺ
events.summary: He was born on a Monday in the Year of the Elephant. The exact day of the month is much disputed; 12 Rabi' al-Awwal is the most widely known date among people, but it is not a certain one.

events.title: He is named Muhammad
events.summary: His grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib named him Muhammad, a name that was less common among the Arabs at that time.

events.title: His nursing with Halimah al-Sa'diyyah
events.summary: It was the custom of the nobles of Mecca to send their children to the desert for eloquence and a healthier environment. Halimah al-Sa'diyyah of Banu Sa'd took him, and he spent his early childhood with her.
events.placeText: Mecca → the desert of Banu Sa'd

events.title: The first splitting of the breast
events.summary: It is reported in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere that Gabriel opened his breast while he was a child, washed and purified his heart, and then restored it as it was.

authenticity.qualifier: as to the origin of the report

events.title: His return to his mother
events.summary: After the period of nursing among Banu Sa'd he returned to his mother Aminah.
events.placeText: The desert of Banu Sa'd → Mecca

events.title: Aminah's visit to Medina
events.summary: Aminah travelled with the Prophet to visit his maternal relatives among Banu al-Najjar, and then returned with him.

events.title: The death of Aminah bint Wahb
events.summary: His mother died at al-Abwa when he was about six years old, leaving him orphaned of both father and mother.

events.title: The guardianship of 'Abd al-Muttalib
events.summary: His grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib took charge of his care after his mother's death.

events.title: The death of 'Abd al-Muttalib
events.summary: His grandfather died when he was about eight, and his guardianship passed to his uncle Abu Talib.

events.title: The guardianship of Abu Talib
events.summary: The Prophet lived in the house of his uncle Abu Talib, who loved and protected him although he never entered Islam.

events.title: The journey to al-Sham with Abu Talib
events.summary: He travelled on a trading journey with his uncle while still young. The sirah literature relates the account of the monk Bahira, but its details are debated in hadith scholarship, so they should not all be presented as certain.

events.title: The Sacrilegious War (Harb al-Fijar)
events.summary: He witnessed part of its events in his youth, and was not a principal combatant in it.

events.title: The Pact of the Virtuous (Hilf al-Fudul)
events.summary: A group of the clans of Quraysh allied to support the wronged and restore rights. The Prophet praised this principle after prophethood.

authenticity.qualifier: as to the origin of the pact

events.title: Trading for Khadijah
events.summary: He worked in the trade of Khadijah bint Khuwaylid and travelled with her capital to al-Sham, becoming known for his trustworthiness and truthfulness.

events.title: His marriage to Khadijah
events.summary: He married her at about twenty-five; she was older than him according to the best-known view. She was his first wife, and he took no other wife while she lived.

events.title: Family and trading life
events.summary: He lived a settled life with Khadijah and had his sons and daughters by her, among them al-Qasim, 'Abdullah, Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah.

events.title: The rebuilding of the Ka'bah
events.summary: Quraysh rebuilt the Ka'bah after it was damaged. When the tribes disputed over who should set the Black Stone in place, they referred the matter to the Prophet. He placed the stone on a cloth, ordered the tribal chiefs to lift it together, and then set it in place with his own hand.

events.title: Seclusion and worship in Hira
events.summary: The Prophet used to withdraw to the cave of Hira and devote himself to worship before the revelation came down.

events.title: The first revelation
events.summary: Gabriel came to the Prophet, and the opening verses of Surat al-'Alaq were revealed: “Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth” (Al-'Alaq 96:1). With this, prophethood began.

events.title: The Prophet's return to Khadijah
events.summary: He returned deeply affected by what had happened; Khadijah reassured him and then took him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal.

events.title: Waraqah ibn Nawfal
events.summary: Waraqah told him that the one who had come to him was the same Namus who had come to the prophets, and that his people would turn against him.

authenticity.qualifier: as to the substance of the account

events.title: Khadijah accepts Islam
events.summary: She was the first of all people to believe in him.

events.title: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib accepts Islam
events.summary: He accepted Islam as a boy, and was living in the Prophet's household at that time.

events.title: Zayd ibn Harithah accepts Islam
events.summary: He was among those closest to the Prophet and among the earliest Muslims.

events.title: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq accepts Islam
events.summary: He was among the first to come to Islam, and afterwards contributed to the conversion of a number of senior Companions.

events.title: The phase of the secret call
events.summary: The mission continued within a limited circle, and the first community of Muslims began to form.

events.title: 'Uthman, al-Zubayr, Talhah, Sa'd and others accept Islam
events.summary: A number of the senior Companions entered Islam during the first years.

events.title: The call is made public
events.summary: The command came to warn his closest kin and to proclaim the message openly, and the Prophet began to call Quraysh publicly.

events.title: Calling Quraysh at al-Safa
events.summary: The Prophet gathered Quraysh and warned them, and the phase of open confrontation began.

events.title: Persecution of the Muslims intensifies
events.summary: The Muslims were subjected to torture, boycott and social pressure, and the most vulnerable among them bore the worst of it.

events.title: The first migration to Abyssinia
events.summary: The Prophet permitted some of his Companions to migrate to Abyssinia, because it had a king under whom no one was wronged.

events.title: The second migration to Abyssinia
events.summary: A larger number of Muslims migrated, and Abyssinia became a refuge for the vulnerable.

events.title: Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib accepts Islam
events.summary: Hamzah's conversion was an important turning point, giving the Prophet strong support from within Banu Hashim.

events.title: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab accepts Islam
events.summary: 'Umar's conversion had a great effect on the strength of the Muslims and their visibility in Mecca.

events.title: The Negus and his stance towards the migrants
events.summary: He refused to hand the Muslims over to Quraysh, and granted them safety in Abyssinia.

authenticity.qualifier: as to the substance of his stance

events.title: The boycott of Banu Hashim
events.summary: Quraysh imposed a social and economic boycott on Banu Hashim and their allies, who were forced to live in the valley of Abu Talib.

events.title: The end of the boycott
events.summary: The blockade ended after years of hardship.

events.title: The death of Abu Talib
events.summary: The Prophet's uncle and his political and social protector in Mecca died, without his acceptance of Islam being established in the sound reports.

events.title: The death of Khadijah
events.summary: Khadijah died; she had been the Prophet's greatest support at the beginning of his mission.

events.title: The Year of Sorrow
events.summary: That period became known as the Year of Sorrow because of the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah, two events that affected the Prophet deeply.

events.title: The journey to Ta'if
events.summary: He went to Ta'if to call Thaqif to Islam. They did not respond to him, and he returned to Mecca.

events.title: A group from Yathrib accepts Islam
events.summary: Some of the people of Yathrib began to accept Islam after meeting the Prophet during the pilgrimage seasons.

events.title: The first pledge of al-'Aqabah
events.summary: A number of the people of Yathrib pledged to the Prophet Islam, obedience and the abandonment of certain prohibited acts — an important step towards the Hijrah.

events.title: Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr is sent
events.summary: The Prophet sent Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr to teach the people of Yathrib the Qur'an and Islam, and a number of them accepted Islam at his hands.

events.title: The second pledge of al-'Aqabah
events.summary: A large number of the people of Yathrib pledged to the Prophet and undertook to support and protect him. This was the political and social basis for the Hijrah.

events.title: Permission to migrate to Medina
events.summary: The Muslims began to migrate to Yathrib, singly and in groups.

events.title: The conspiracy of Quraysh
events.summary: Quraysh gathered to be rid of the Prophet. Permission to depart was then given, and the Prophet set out with Abu Bakr.

events.title: The Hijrah
events.summary: The Prophet set out with Abu Bakr. They made for the cave of Thawr, and then took an unusual route towards Medina.

events.title: Staying in the cave
events.summary: The Prophet and Abu Bakr remained in the cave for several nights, then continued on their way.

events.title: The account of Suraqah ibn Malik
events.summary: Suraqah set out in pursuit of the Prophet hoping for the reward, then realised that God was protecting His prophet, and returned without directing Quraysh to him.

events.title: Arrival at Quba
events.summary: The Prophet reached Quba, stayed several days, and the mosque of Quba was built.

events.title: Entering Medina
events.summary: The Prophet entered Yathrib and its people received him; the city came to be known as al-Madinah.

events.title: Building the Prophet's Mosque
events.summary: Construction began on the mosque that became the centre of worship, teaching and administration in the new Muslim community.

events.title: The brotherhood between the Muhajirun and the Ansar
events.summary: The Prophet established brotherhood between the emigrants and the helpers, strengthening social and economic bonds.

events.title: Ordering the community of Medina / the Sahifah
events.summary: Relations between the different groups in Medina were regulated, defining mutual rights, duties and responsibilities.

events.title: The beginning of Medinan legislation
events.summary: Rulings concerning the community, prayer, fasting, zakat, jihad, family and transactions began to be revealed in greater detail.

events.title: The change of the qiblah
events.summary: The prayer direction changed from Jerusalem to the Sacred Mosque — an event of great religious significance in forming the identity of the Muslim community.

events.title: The Battle of Badr
events.summary: The Muslims set out originally to intercept a Quraysh caravan; the encounter then turned into a battle with the army of Quraysh. The Muslims numbered about 300, and the battle ended in their victory. Its well-known date is **17 Ramadan 2 AH / 13 March 624 CE**.

events.title: Captives and losses among the leaders of Quraysh
events.summary: A number of the foremost leaders of Quraysh were killed and others taken captive, which had a great political effect on the conflict.

events.title: The expedition against Banu Qaynuqa'
events.summary: It took place after Badr amid rising political and military tension within Medina, and ended with the departure of Banu Qaynuqa' from the city according to the traditional historical accounts.

events.title: Quraysh prepares for Uhud
events.summary: After Badr, Quraysh assembled a large army under Abu Sufyan and marched on Medina.

events.title: The Battle of Uhud
events.summary: The Muslims went out to meet the army of Quraysh. When some of the archers left their positions the Muslim ranks broke; Hamzah and a number of the Companions were killed, and the Prophet was wounded.

events.title: The expedition of Hamra al-Asad
events.summary: The Prophet and the Muslims went out after Uhud in a show of pursuit of Quraysh, to make clear that the Muslims had not collapsed.

events.title: The expedition against Banu al-Nadir
events.summary: It ended with the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir from Medina, in the context of a dispute over the treaty and political relations.

events.title: The expedition of Dhat al-Riqa'
events.summary: The Prophet went out on a campaign in Najd, and the reports mention various events connected with it.

events.title: The expedition of Badr al-Maw'id
events.summary: The Muslims went out to Badr in fulfilment of an earlier appointment with Quraysh, but Quraysh did not engage.

events.title: The expedition of Dumat al-Jandal
events.summary: The Prophet went north after reports of hostile gatherings, and returned without a major battle.

events.title: The Battle of the Confederates (the Trench)
events.summary: Quraysh and many tribes allied and besieged Medina. Salman al-Farisi proposed digging the trench, a defensive method unfamiliar to the Arabs at that time.

events.title: The failure of the siege
events.summary: The siege continued and then the confederates withdrew without achieving their aim. This was a major turning point in the balance of power.

events.title: The expedition against Banu Qurayzah
events.summary: It took place immediately after the Confederates, in the context of the reports concerning the breaking of the treaty during the siege, and ended with the judgement passed on the men of the tribe as recorded in the traditional sources. This event in particular has detailed historical and juristic dimensions and multiple accounts, and should be studied separately if you wish to go into it further.

events.title: The shift from confrontation to negotiation
events.summary: After the Confederates the balance of power changed, and the Prophet became able to take the political initiative rather than merely defend.

events.title: Setting out for al-Hudaybiyah
events.summary: The Prophet set out with about 1,400 of his Companions intending the 'umrah, not battle.

events.title: Quraysh blocks the Muslims from entering Mecca
events.summary: Quraysh sent representatives to negotiate, and lengthy negotiations followed.

events.title: The Pledge of Ridwan
events.summary: The Companions pledged to the Prophet under the tree to stand firm, after an unconfirmed report spread that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan had been killed.

events.title: The Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah
events.summary: A truce was agreed. Among its main terms were that the Muslims would return that year and be permitted the 'umrah the following year. To some of the Companions the treaty appeared outwardly to be a concession, but it opened a wide phase of contact and expansion. The Qur'an described the treaty as “a signal victory” (Al-Fath 48:1).

events.title: Letters to kings and rulers
events.summary: The Prophet sent letters calling a number of rulers to Islam, among them Heraclius, Khosrow, the Muqawqis and the Negus.

events.title: The expedition of Khaybar
events.summary: The Muslims marched on Khaybar. The fighting ended with the capture of its fortresses and arrangements concerning its people and their lands.

events.title: 'Ali at Khaybar
events.summary: The Prophet gave the banner to 'Ali at one stage of the fighting, and important events in the capture of the fortresses took place at his hands.

events.title: The compensatory 'umrah
events.summary: The Prophet and his Companions entered Mecca and performed the 'umrah in accordance with what had been agreed at al-Hudaybiyah.

events.title: The Battle of Mu'tah
events.summary: The Prophet sent an army north. Its three commanders — Zayd ibn Harithah, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah — were killed, and Khalid ibn al-Walid then took command and reorganised the army.

events.title: Khalid ibn al-Walid and 'Amr ibn al-'As accept Islam
events.summary: A number of important figures accepted Islam at the end of the Meccan period and the beginning of the later Medinan period; the conversion of Khalid and 'Amr had a great effect on the phase that followed.

events.title: The breaking of the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah
events.summary: Allies of Quraysh attacked allies of the Muslims, which was regarded as a breach of the treaty, and Quraysh began to lose its ability to hold the agreement together.

events.title: The march on Mecca
events.summary: The Prophet set out for Mecca with a large army, said to have numbered around 10,000 fighters.

events.title: The conquest of Mecca
events.summary: The Muslims entered Mecca, for the most part without major fighting. The Prophet declared safety for the people, entered the Sacred Mosque, and the idols around the Ka'bah were removed.

events.title: Abu Sufyan accepts Islam
events.summary: Abu Sufyan accepted Islam before the Muslims entered Mecca, and afterwards became one of the senior Companions.

events.title: The general amnesty
events.summary: The Prophet declared safety for many of those who had fought against him — among the most notable moral and political acts of the conquest of Mecca.

events.title: The Battle of Hunayn
events.summary: Hawazin and Thaqif went out against the Muslims. There was disorder at the start of the battle; the Muslims then re-formed their ranks, and the battle ended in their victory.

events.title: The siege of Ta'if
events.summary: The Muslims moved on Ta'if after Hunayn and besieged it, then withdrew without taking it in that campaign.

events.title: Tribal delegations accept Islam after the conquest
events.summary: The conquest of Mecca brought a rapid shift in the balance of power, and the tribes began to enter Islam or to send delegations to Medina.

events.title: The expedition of Tabuk
events.summary: The Prophet marched north with a large army because of reports of a Byzantine and Ghassanid threat. No major battle took place directly, but the campaign demonstrated the reach of the Muslim state.

events.title: The trial of those who stayed behind from Tabuk
events.summary: Surat al-Tawbah relates the account of three Companions who stayed behind and then told the Prophet the truth about what had happened; the acceptance of their repentance was revealed afterwards.

events.title: The Year of Delegations
events.summary: Delegations began arriving in Medina from across the Arabian Peninsula to declare Islam or to reach agreement with the Muslim state.

events.title: Abu Bakr leads the pilgrimage
events.summary: Abu Bakr went out as leader of the hajj; the Prophet then sent 'Ali with verses of Surat al-Tawbah to announce the ending of certain treaties and conditions relating to the polytheists.

events.title: Islam spreads across most of the Peninsula
events.summary: Medina became a political and religious centre to which most of the tribes of the Peninsula were connected, and delegations arrived to declare Islam and allegiance.

events.title: The expedition of Usamah ibn Zayd
events.summary: The Prophet equipped an army under Usamah ibn Zayd to march north. This was in the last days of his life, and the army did not set out while he lived, because of his illness.

events.title: Setting out for the Farewell Pilgrimage
events.summary: The Prophet left Medina for the hajj, and a vast gathering of Muslims joined him.

events.title: The Farewell Pilgrimage
events.summary: The Prophet performed the rites of the hajj and taught the people the rites; it was his last pilgrimage.

events.title: The Farewell Sermon
events.summary: He affirmed the inviolability of life, property and honour, enjoined good treatment of women, declared many practices of the Jahiliyyah abolished, and affirmed the brotherhood of Muslims.

events.title: The verse on the completion of the religion
events.summary: The verse was revealed: “This day have I perfected your religion for you…” (Al-Ma'idah 5:3) — in the context of the Farewell Pilgrimage.

events.title: The return to Medina
events.summary: The Prophet returned to Medina after completing the pilgrimage.

events.title: The onset of the Prophet's illness
events.summary: His illness grew severe, and he asked his wives' permission to be nursed in the house of 'A'ishah, which they granted.

events.title: Abu Bakr leads the prayer
events.summary: When the Prophet's illness grew severe he ordered Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer, one of the significant events of his final days.

events.title: The Prophet looks out upon the Muslims at prayer
events.summary: On one of the days of his illness he drew back the curtain and looked at the Companions praying behind Abu Bakr, then returned to his chamber.

events.title: The death of the Prophet ﷺ
events.summary: He died in the house of 'A'ishah at about sixty-three lunar years of age. 12 Rabi' al-Awwal is the best-known date, but the determination of the Hijri day is disputed. Modern historical sources date the death to 8 June 632 CE.

date.hijri: 12 Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH, according to the best-known view

events.title: His burial
events.summary: He was buried in the place where he died, in the chamber of 'A'ishah, which later became part of the Prophet's Mosque.
